To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the carboxyl-terminal (C-terminal) region of the HCMV IE1 protein disrupts type II interferon (IFN) signaling.
the carboxy terminal region of the HCMV IE1 protein disrupts IFN signaling.
the carboxyl-terminal portion of the HCMV IE1 protein disrupts type II interferon signaling by interacting with STAT2, and that this interaction is required for IE1-mediated ND10 disruption.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the immediate early 2 (IE2) protein of HCMV in IFNγ-mediated signaling.
the role of the IE1 protein in IFNγ-mediated immune signaling.
the molecular mechanisms that are used by the HCMV IE1 protein to interfere with type II IFN signaling.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the C-terminal domain of HCMV IE1 interacts with STAT2 and disrupts IFN signaling by preventing the formation of the IFN-activated STAT1-STAT2 heterodimer.
the carboxyl-terminal portion of IE1 is necessary for disruption of interferon signaling.
IE1 disruptes IFNγ signaling through a novel mechanism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the C-terminal portion of the IE1 protein disrupts IFN signaling by interfering with the interaction of STAT2 and IFNγ-activated STAT2 (ISGF-3).
the carboxyl-terminal portion of IE1 is responsible for disruption of IFN signaling, and this is not a result of ND10 disruption.
the IE1 C-terminus is required for IFNγ signaling disruption and that this disruption does not appear to be due to a direct association with STAT1.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the carboxy-terminal region of the IE1 protein of HCMV disrupts IFN signaling.
the carboxyl terminal region of the HCMV immediate early 1 protein (IE1) disrupts type II interferon signaling by interfering with the function of STAT2.
IE1 disrupt IFNγ signaling.
